statement: Every partition of the vertices that cannot be improved by moving a single vertex to the other side is a maximum cut.
definitions: Setting: a finite simple undirected unweighted graph G; a partition of V(G) into two sides (either may be empty); the cut value is the number of edges with endpoints on different sides. 'Cannot be improved by moving a single vertex' means no move of one vertex to the other side strictly increases the cut value. Maximum cut = partition of maximum cut value.
ground_truth_witness: The 4-cycle C4 on V = {a,b,c,d} with edges ab, bc, cd, da, and the partition ({a,b}, {c,d}). Its cut contains bc and da, value 2. Flipping any single vertex leaves the cut value at 2 (flipping a gives cut {ab, bc}, flipping b gives {ab, da}, and symmetrically for c, d), so the partition is a single-flip local optimum. The maximum cut is ({a,c}, {b,d}) with all 4 edges cut, so the local optimum attains exactly the tight factor 1/2.
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records

skeptic.objection: False and the C4 witness is valid: partition {a,b}|{c,d} has value 2, all four single flips leave the value at 2 (so no strict improvement), and the max cut is 4. The statement omits the graph and the meaning of 'improved' (strict increase) and of the cut value (edge count); pin these. Small construction with a real local check; roster has no max-cut / local-search item.
